item.title: It's An Anomalous World: Re: It's An Anomalous World
item.content:encoded: Hart Island. An uninhabited island near NYC that's been home to a barracks, a POW camp, a mental asylum, a sanitarium, a homeless shelter, a reformatory school, a rehab center, and a prison, now used as a mass grave for unclaimed and unidentified remains, miscarriages, and stillbirths. The burials here are carried out by inmates, and the bodies are frequently mixed up and put in the wrong plots. Past a certain point, no more records exist of who's buried where. It's borderline impossible to visit, since it's still part of the Department of Corrections, and the waters around it are treacherous and full of rocks. Nothing inherently anomalous about any of that, but the negative energy around this place must be insane.

item.title: Flashpoint Just league Dark: Re: Flashpoint Just league Dark
item.content:encoded:
It's up to interpretation but since DC is a multiverse, I'd think it's an alternative reality, not a reset (sorry). We may think it's a reset when really, Barry has simply jumped from one reality to another.

Compare it to endgame. In that, the Avengers travel to the past to take the infinity stones to the future. In doing so, they cause alterations to the past but the future remains unchanged. This is because, at the moment they go back in time, to preserve the flow of time, the universe creates an alternative universe. This is to prevent a paradox. You're no longer altering the past because it's no longer your past. The same can be said for JLD.

In Flashpoint, barry travels back and creates an alternative reality in which his mother survives and a whole loud of s*** goes down. He then does this again and supposedly resets the universe back to what it was. He hasn't. He's now created a third alternative universe which is seemingly identical to the first. In JLD, he's now doing it a fourth time.

Unfortunately, if you want to avoid paradoxes and have as much logic in time travel, it's got to be alternative worlds. Reset just isn't possible.

item.title: Is there any websites similar to the SCP Wiki?: Re: Is there any websites similar to the SCP Wiki?
item.content:encoded:
The Wayward Society.

The Wayward Society is a volunteer organization dedicated to the eradication and investigation of dangerous, paranormal, and otherwise anomalous entities. Here, you will find documentation on the findings of those who have risked their lives or sacrificed themselves for this goal.

Its creed and mission is kinda similar to our Wiki, but unlike others it's not directly derived from SCPF (at least inspired by it, say).

Personal perspective: WwdS is more "classical" and gives an undertone of early-modern mystical, uncanny fantasies and while Foundation relies more on modern sci & tech and resembles hardcore sci-fi.

item.title: It's An Anomalous World: Re: It's An Anomalous World
item.content:encoded:
A shark born without skin or teeth was recently caught by a fishing trawler off the coast of Sardinia. Though dead by the time it was discovered in the trawler's haul, has been estimated to be about 3 years old, and an otherwise healthy example of the blackmouth catshark species.

It is currently believed that its condition was simply a very weird genetic mutation, but researchers are looking into possible pollution factors as well, whether as a congenital cause or as a cause for the mutation.

The reason for the lack of teeth ties into some interesting secondary real-world weirdness: the teeth of sharks and their evolutionary siblings are essentially really big scales that use some of the standard procedural programming for chordate teeth They grow from the gums rather than the jaw- ergo, no gums, no teeth. When you see those megalodon jaws with teeth, the jaw is usually more like a really fancy display case: even in the rare cases where a preserved jaw is found with it's original teeth, there's nothing to hold them in place except some grooves.

item.title: Is there any websites similar to the SCP Wiki?: Re: Is there any websites similar to the SCP Wiki?
item.content:encoded:
Hello, YellowISlol here!

My reply!
...

Well, as a member of The Backrooms community, as well as a staff member from over there, it felt like I should point that out over anything else. Recently, we've been getting some traction from the SCP wiki, which is always good!

The jist of The Backrooms is what it says on the tin; The Backrooms. However, in the case of The Backrooms, it is a creative interpretation of The Backrooms, where there are more than a single, or three levels, all of which vary wildly. Each Level is vaguely reminiscent of The Frontrooms (which is our universe), and are built upon using Entities. Entities are creatures which can be found wandering some Levels. Some take up a majority of the Levels, well some may be unique to a specific Level. We have a wide selection of tales and canons (I actually made The Council Canon, and am working on expanding upon it more and more), and we also feature objects, which are kind of what they say on the tin.

We, similar to here, are a community of writers. I personally have written quite a bit over there1, and am working on writing more. We aren't as focused on narrative relating to the Levels themself, however, our canons expand upon the lore of The Backrooms greatly, including the most recent one, the Industrialization canon. This one in particular has been gaining quite a bit of traction.

If I were to recommend you some works to start, I would definitely say Level 0, the original Backrooms made off the 4chan post. However, there are many more works then this which are all decent, which I'll list as follows:

Levels
  • Level 6 is one of the most "dark-esq" based Levels on the site, and was written with this intention in mind. Filled with illusions and terror, insanity comes commonly to wanderers here…
  • Level 18 has always been known for being a weird one, but I recently rewrote this one to be much more prominently connected. This Level is based upon your childhood memories, and degrades at your sanity through this process.
  • Level 178 is my personal favorite article on the site, for good reason to. It is one of the most in-depth on the site, and resembles a Chinese home. This one is highly recommended from me, though that may be personal preference.
  • Level 241 is one of the strangest ones on the site, but it was executed in a perfect way. This Level may be hard to grasp, but it's all within a especially hairy dog, and is a dog pound.
  • Level 666 may be a controversial pick, at least for site standards, as many believe that hell within The Backrooms isn't the best pick. However, the interpretation, as well as the execution is what makes me truly love this Level. I was one who actually pushed for its feature.
  • Level 777 was written by me, but it has to be included in this. As it stands, this is the longest Level on the site, so you'll be in for a wild ride. I'm actually writing a Level twice this length rn, so I'll include that when the time comes. As it stands for now, however, infinite gambling is infinite gambling.
  • Level 999 is the last Level I'll include off the positive Levels list, due to it being the last Level in cluster 1. I personally don't enjoy this, though I can see the appeal, so I leave it here.
  • Level -4 is the first negative Level I'll include. It's short, but it captures the essence of a negative Level well, and shows you the theme they follow. For negative Levels, I recommend this one first.
  • Level -13 was released recently, but its a perfect example of horror without danger, and is one I personally I critted. I recommend you read this one heavily.
  • Level -183 is another one I wrote, but is a perfect example of a negative Level which breaks the norms. It is likely the least dangerous negative Level out, and will retain this for a while, but its a great start for a GoI, Backrooms Robotics (which I made to :P)
  • Level 9.1 is the first Sub-l+Layer I'm gonna recommend, due to it being an example of expanding upon the host Levels lore, which is something I love within Sub-Layers.
  • Level 178.1 I wrote this to This one is yet another example of a Sub-Layer which expands upon it's host layers lore, which I like to summarize as "Where do all the monsters go?"
  • Level fun =) an iconic one, and is one of the few examples of altering Entities, which is something I love.
  • The Blue Channel expands upon the concept of infinity in such a unique way, which is why I fought for it to be featured (and it was!).
  • The Oxygen Ocean is a controversial pick. Not for the Level itself, but for the fact that I'm not listing it as a tale. However, for this sake, it's listed as a Level. It expands upon the Leviathan, which is my favorite Entity 1 proposal.
Entities
  • The Leviathan is my favorite Entity 1 proposal, with good reason to. It's vague, mysterious, yet it captures the essence of Entity 1 so well.
  • Smilers are a strange Entity, and are mysteriously horrifying. I have mixed feelings about putting them here, but they are quite apparent in many Levels, so it's effectively a given to include it here.
  • Jerry is a parrot who influences the minds of others greatly, making his own cult like group. This is one of the more meme based entries, but it is written very well nevertheless, and is deserving of a spot on this list.
  • Insanites. This is only included on the list due to its reference in many articles. Concept-wise, this was written very well, but the execution is tame. I am only including this due to its significance. Moving on.
  • The Artist. Same as above, but I enjoy this one more :3
  • The Partygoers =) are a very famous Entity, due largely due to their creepy yet cute persona, as well as their unique take on software edits. Highly recommended.
  • Koko is a self insert is a very unique Entity in that it doesn't reside on Levels, but rather, the internet within The Backrooms. Highly recommended, as it grasp the concept of AI pretty well.
  • The Game Master is, by far, the most iconic on the site, clocking in second highest rated, only beaten by Level 0 itself. The Game Master is highly controversial, however, it is a rare case of an Entity which has higher status then the Level, and is executed in a marvelous way.
  • The Dollmaker is quite a sad Entity, and was made quite recently. It took the negative aspects of The Game Master and made them much more likeable, and overall is considered one of my favorites.
  • The Plush Dino is one of the cutest Entities on the site, and is written with that in mind. This is one of the few Entities which are non-dangerous, and actively want to be helpful in any way they can.
  • Cheshires finish off the list well, and are quite gimmicky! They are adorable little creatures, and I love them a lot!
Tales
  • Emergency Broadcast starts the list. I won't go in depth on tales, as they are much better read blind, unless they relate to something in particular.
  • the game master is dead... HELP ME. Otherworld tale
  • M.E.G. The Discovery of the Insanity.

…I don't read tales as much, if you can't tell…

Objects

Objects are meant to be read blind, so no description will be provided. As stated above, they are simply objects found throughout The Backrooms, but they aren't always what they seem…

  • Almond Water
  • Firesalt
  • Royal Rations
  • Lamps
  • Cashew Water
  • The Everything Machine
  • Super Almond Water
  • WiFi
  • Level Keys

I hope you consider checking out The Backrooms Wiki, we'd love to have you!
